$comment: D-LANG-DIRECT-CALL-INT-POINTEE-COMPAT (TF-C135) — the RUNTIME witness for the widened integer-pointee pointer-arg admission at a DIRECT call. TF-C41 admitted `long long*` into a `ptr<i64>` parameter only when the callee was minted from a SHIPPED FFI DESCRIPTOR; that gate keyed the decision on where the DECLARATION came from rather than on what the TYPES are, and a real header hits the identical shape: on Darwin/LP64 `tcl.h` takes its `#ifdef __APPLE__`/`#ifdef __LP64__` override, defines TCL_WIDE_INT_IS_LONG, and declares `Tcl_WideInt` as `long` while `sqlite3_int64` is `long long`. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-07: upstream sqlite's `ext/session/test_session.c:1744` `Tcl_GetWideIntFromObj(interp, objv[4], &iVal)` compiles under Apple clang 21.0.0 with exactly one `-Wincompatible-pointer-types` WARNING and rc=0 on all four macOS SDKs present (MacOSX13.3/14.4/15.4/26.5), while DSS emitted a hard error[S0003] — so BOTH mach-o legs failed to build their testfixture on EVERY host (WSL, macOS and the arm64 VPS each reproduced it independently). DSS now warns (S_IncompatiblePointerIntegerPointee, 0xE060) instead of refusing, matching gcc, clang and MSVC C4133; `--warnings-as-errors` restores the strict posture. ★ THE PAIR IS SELECTED PER DATA MODEL (`__LP64__`, declared by the object FORMAT) BECAUSE NO PAIR OF C INTEGER TYPES IS SAME-REPRESENTATION EVERYWHERE: `long`/`long long` collide only on LP64, `int`/`long` only on LLP64. A single hard-coded pair would leave the other data model compiling a different, uninteresting program while still reporting green — the vacuous-arm failure. ★ THE ADMISSION REALIZES A Ptr→Ptr BITCAST, WHICH LOWERS TO NOTHING, so 'it compiled' proves almost nothing: every shape here has the CALLEE store and `main` read back, and the array-element, read-modify-write and negative-value shapes exist so a bitcast that lost an index, a stale slot, or a wrong-width/wrong-signedness store changes the exit code rather than passing quietly. exitCode 42 = all four shapes agreed; any other value is a BITMASK naming which broke (1 scalar, 2 array element, 4 read-modify-write, 8 negative).
